What pass requires: Every question a student answers in the packet appears on a slide in the packet's own words, with the packet page named on that slide, and every slide that sends students to write names its page. Fail = a packet question missing from the slides, reworded, or a writing slide with no page named.
Notes: The deck checker compares the deck to the packet (packet.json or the packet .docx); the judge reads its report and spot-checks.

What pass requires: No slide shows an answer key before its reveal, look-fors, notes on likely mistakes, assessment rationale, or directions addressed to the teacher. Answers appear only behind a reveal step the teacher triggers. Fail = any of these visible on a slide.

Criterion: Every slide carries something to look at
What pass requires: Every slide gives a student something to learn from in ten seconds without the teacher's voice: a real number with its comparison, a photograph of the actual thing, a structure with parts (cards, steps, two sides), a named specific, or a question with a hard edge. No slide is a headline over a paragraph, and no summary line sits under a slide's body. Fail = any slide that is only a headline, or a paragraph, or a restatement.

Every fixed-length block (do-now, talk moves, work blocks, closing) has a countdown the room can see, matching the plan's minutes; timers start when the teacher starts them. Fail = a fixed-length block with no timer, or timers that disagree with the plan.

Every chart, data result, or answer students should reason about stays hidden until the class commits to a guess (a vote, a written prediction, a partner agreement), and the reveal explains in a sentence a student could repeat. Fail = a result shown before any prediction, or a reveal with no explanation.

Each talk move in the plan has a slide carrying the question, each partner's job, a speaking stem, a phased timer (think, A talks, B talks), and who reports. Fail = a talk move with no slide, or a talk slide missing its question, roles, stem, or timer.

Each game round is a fair guess (a student could reason toward it without already knowing it), its reveal explains, its answer and every sort card's bin agree with the packet's answer key, and teams and points appear only when the teacher asked for them. Fail = any round that fails one of these.

Each of the lesson's key words has a word slide (the word, how to say it, a one-sentence meaning, a picture or non-example) and is marked once on each slide that uses it. Fail = a key word with no word slide, or unmarked where it is used.

When the class has home languages, every slide that asks a question or gives a direction carries the packet's line for that question in each language, word for word, tagged with its language so read-aloud uses the right voice. Fail = a missing, untagged, or reworded line.

Every photograph shows the thing the slide's headline claims, cropped so the subject is in frame, with real alt text and a credit, from an openly licensed source. Fail = a photograph that only matches the topic, a missing alt text or credit, or a decorative image.
Notes: The deck checker verifies alt text, credits and crops; the judge decides whether each photograph argues for its claim.

What pass requires: The deck is one file that runs from the teacher's computer with keyboard and click control: no student devices, accounts, or logins, no student names, and media linked by URL with a fallback when a link fails. Fail = anything that needs a student device or account, a student's name in the file, or a slide that breaks without its link.

The deck is built in the same turn only when the teacher asked for slides or a standing request says every lesson gets one; otherwise it is offered as a next move. Fail = a deck built unasked, or no offer when none was built.
